newsitem.title: UK: UK Conservatives pledge to spend more on health.
newsitem.headline: UK Conservatives pledge to spend more on health.

text.p: Britain's ruling Conservative Party pledged on Wednesday to continue increasing spending on the National Health Service.
"We will continue, year by year, to increase the real resources committed to the NHS, so NHS spending will continue to share in a growing economy," the Conservatives' election manifesto said.
The election is set for May 1 and the Conservatives lag badly in the opinion polls, although the latest one suggests the gap may be narrowing.
A poll in the Guardian newspaper on Wednesday put the opposition Labour Party's lead down at 14 percentage points.

A Conservative government would continue to rely on the Private Finance Initiative -- a scheme to encourage the private sector to invest in infrastructure projects -- for much of the upgrading of the NHS.
"We will promote the Private Finance Initiative which will unleash a new flow of investment funds into the modernisation of the NHS," the manifesto said.
PFI projects have been slow to take off. Some 23 hospital schemes had named approved bidders by the end of last year but only two had agreed commercial terms and no final contracts had been signed.

The Tory manifesto said a Conservative government would publish more information on how successfully hospitals are treating patients and would allow family doctors to provide a wider range of healthcare services from their surgeries.
Nurses will also be allowed to prescribe a wider range of drugs and the Conservatives want to see more nurses qualifying.
"The number of nurses qualifying each year will increase by 2,500 within the next five years," the manifesto said.
It also said medical school intakes would rise by 5,000 a year by the turn of the century.
